target_customer: Twitch streamers and esports broadcasters looking to engage and monetize fans
problem: Streamers had few tools to reward loyal viewers and turn engagement into repeat viewing and subscriptions. Revlo let broadcasters issue a custom virtual currency redeemable for rewards.
business_model: Freemium streamer tools with monetization features; sustainable model not found
product_category: Creator economy and live stream fan loyalty

founders.name: James Sun
founders.background_notes: BetaKit calls him a lifelong gamer. Listed as a co-founder in Twitch deal coverage.

founders.name: Adam Hueniken
founders.background_notes: The only founder shown on the YC page.

founders.name: Julie Topp
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in coverage of the Twitch hire.

exit.reason: Team joined Twitch; the Pursuit and Revlo services were shut down effective 2018-12-17 and the product and IP were not acquired

technical_complexity.rationale: Chat integration and a points and rewards system on Twitch APIs. Scale across thousands of channels was the main challenge.

defensibility.rationale: Streamer bots and extensions could add loyalty points easily, and Twitch itself later added channel points.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitch, the platform, hired the team in December 2018 and did not take the product.

market_need_then: During beta Revlo reported 15,000 broadcasters reaching over 5 million monthly unique viewers, and one streamer reported 45 percent longer view time (company-cited via BetaKit).

branding.domain_note: revlo.co is now a parked placeholder that may be for sale.

identity.voice_and_tone: Gamer and streamer oriented; custom currency names such as AmazeBalls

rebrands.why: not found; Twitch coverage describes Pursuit as formerly Revlo

branding.community_and_virality: Press (Engadget, GamesBeat, BetaKit) covered Revlo and a streamer community blog discussed it, but no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within Twitch streamer circles and trade press, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.why: not stated in sources found; the Pursuit analytics platform was shut down with the Twitch deal

outcome_analysis: Revlo raised a $1.12 million seed in May 2016 and showed strong early broadcaster adoption, but it depended on Twitch and, per the CEO, struggled to find a sustainable business model. In December 2018 Twitch hired the founders and first employee, and the products were shut down on December 17, 2018 without product or IP transfer. This is a soft-landing team hire rather than an exit for the product.
notes: Company status Acquired on YC. A second seed of $2M in October 2016 appears only on StartupIntros (aggregator) and CB Insights totals $1.34M, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round.
